newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down, more falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down, more falls seen.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down at or near intraday lows on Friday, dragged by long liquidation in the morning and short-selling late in the session with technical charts showing a downward trend, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 23,640 yuan ($2,850) per tonne, losing 160 yuan. It opened at a high of 23,820 yuan per tonne.
June fell 170 yuan to 22,980, July 150 to 23,260, August 130 to 23,470, October 110 to 23,720 and November 130 to 23,700.
Combined volume rose to 58,550 tonnes from 36,270 tonnes.
"After continued falls over the past few days, upward lines on technical charts have been totally destroyed, which strengthened investors' determination to build short positions," one trader said.

The London Metal Exchange's (LME) technical charts have being showing signs of over-buying for 10 successive days, indicating heavy pressure for a correction, traders said, adding this has also helped push down local red metal trends.
"The LME charts indicate a correction is due," said another trader.
"After the correction, prices are unlikely to rise sharply, and this will be behind some short-term liquidation on the local market," he said.

LME prices were expected to consolidate around $2,500 a tonne, with a breach of $2,550 necessary for more upside momentum, analysts in London said. Thursday's close was $2,530/33, with the 10-day moving average at $2,502 seen reinforcing the floor.
The price of physical copper in the Shanghai area is around 23,300 yuan per tonne, traders said.
They said they expected copper to find support at the 23,300 to 23,400 yuan in the current round of falls.
Aluminium ended mixed. June did not trade, July fell 200 to 15,300 yuan per tonne and August rose 130 to 15,690 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 280 tonnes from 590 tonnes.
